items.front: In Amazon S3, the read pattern of the objects is unknown and changes over time. Which storage class do you choose?
items.extra: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the class for [unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns](../facts/s3.md#s3-intelligent-tiering-ideal-for-unknown-access).

items.front: In Amazon S3, Standard-IA or One Zone-IA: which one is for the only copy of data?
items.extra: Use S3 Standard-IA for the [primary or only copy of data](../facts/s3.md#s3-standard-ia-vs-one-zone-ia-use). S3 One Zone-IA is [not resilient to the physical loss](../facts/s3.md#s3-standard-ia-vs-one-zone-ia-use) of its Availability Zone.

items.front: In Amazon S3, can you read an S3 Glacier Deep Archive object with a plain GET?
items.back: No. Restore a temporary copy first.
items.extra: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval objects are [immediately available using GET](../facts/s3.md#s3-archive-restore-needed-flexible-deep). For Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive, you first [retrieve data using the RestoreObject REST API](../facts/s3.md#s3-archive-restore-needed-flexible-deep).

items.front: In S3 Object Lock, governance mode or compliance mode: which one can a user with special permission bypass?
items.extra: In governance mode, users cannot delete a locked version [unless they have special permissions](../facts/s3.md#s3-object-lock-governance-mode). The permission is [s3:BypassGovernanceRetention](../facts/s3.md#s3-object-lock-governance-mode).

items.front: In Amazon S3, does a new replication rule copy the objects that already exist?
items.extra: Live replication [replicates newly uploaded objects as they are written](../facts/s3.md#s3-batch-replication-for-existing-objects). S3 Batch Replication [allows you to replicate existing objects](../facts/s3.md#s3-batch-replication-for-existing-objects).

items.front: In Amazon S3, S3 encrypts the data at rest, but the company keeps the encryption keys outside AWS. Which option fits?
items.extra: With SSE-C, S3 encrypts and decrypts the data, and [you retain control of the encryption keys](../facts/s3.md#s3-faq-sse-c-keys). [Starting April 2026](../facts/s3.md#s3-sse-c-disabled-by-default-2026-04), [SSE-C is disabled by default](../facts/s3.md#s3-sse-c-disabled-by-default-2026-04) on new buckets, so you turn it on first.

items.front: In Amazon S3, can a lifecycle rule move an object from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval back to S3 Standard?
items.back: No. Restore it, then copy it.
items.extra: Lifecycle transitions follow [a waterfall model for transitioning between storage classes](../facts/s3.md#s3-lifecycle-transition-waterfall), toward colder classes. To change the class of an archived object, [make a temporary copy of the object first](../facts/s3.md#s3-lifecycle-no-transition-out-of-archive), then copy it with the new class.

items.front: In Amazon S3, can one PUT request upload an object larger than 5 GB?
items.extra: One PUT uploads an object of up to [5 GB](../facts/s3.md#s3-single-put-max). Multipart upload handles larger objects.

items.front: In Amazon S3, bucket policy or object ACL: which one does AWS recommend for access control?
items.back: The bucket policy. Keep ACLs disabled.
items.extra: AWS recommends that you [keep ACLs disabled](../facts/s3.md#s3-acls-not-recommended) unless you need to [control access for each object individually](../facts/s3.md#s3-acls-not-recommended).

items.front: In Amazon S3, can a public bucket policy make objects public while Block Public Access is on?
items.back: No. Block Public Access overrides it.
items.extra: Block Public Access [settings override these policies and permissions](../facts/s3.md#s3-block-public-access-overrides-policies).

items.front: In Amazon S3, does eleven nines of durability protect against an accidental delete?
items.extra: S3 durability [does not protect against accidental or malicious deletes](../facts/s3.md#s3-faq-durability-not-delete-protection).

items.front: In a versioned S3 bucket, a DELETE with or without a version ID: which one adds a delete marker?
items.back: The DELETE without a version ID.
items.extra: A DELETE without a version ID means [issuing a soft delete of the object](../facts/s3.md#s3-delete-marker-soft-delete). The delete marker [becomes the current (or newest) version](../facts/s3.md#s3-delete-marker-soft-delete).

items.front: In Amazon S3, can a versioned bucket go back to unversioned?
items.back: No. You can suspend versioning instead.
items.extra: After you enable versioning, the bucket [can never return to an unversioned state](../facts/s3.md#s3-versioning-never-back-to-unversioned).

items.front: In Amazon S3, users on other continents upload slowly to one central bucket. What do you turn on?
items.extra: Transfer Acceleration fits customers who [upload to a centralized general purpose bucket](../facts/s3.md#s3-transfer-acceleration-when-to-use) from all over the world.

items.front: In Amazon S3, you share a dataset and the downloaders must pay for their downloads. What do you turn on?
items.extra: With Requester Pays, [the requester instead of the bucket owner pays](../facts/s3.md#s3-requester-pays-who-pays) for requests and downloads. For storage, [the bucket owner always pays the cost](../facts/s3.md#s3-requester-pays-who-pays).

items.front: In Amazon S3, can you use an Expedited retrieval for S3 Glacier Deep Archive?
items.extra: For S3 Glacier Deep Archive, Expedited retrieval is [not available](../facts/s3.md#s3-retrieval-expedited-1-5-minutes-not-deep-archive).

items.front: In Amazon S3, which storage class gives single-digit millisecond access in one Availability Zone?
items.extra: S3 Express One Zone is a [single-zone](../facts/s3.md#s3-express-one-zone-single-digit-ms-single-az) class built for [single-digit millisecond data access](../facts/s3.md#s3-express-one-zone-single-digit-ms-single-az).

items.front: In Amazon S3, does a new default encryption setting re-encrypt the objects already in the bucket?
items.back: No. Only new objects use it.
items.extra: The encryption of the objects [in the bucket is not changed](../facts/s3.md#s3-default-encryption-change-not-retroactive). To re-encrypt them, [you can use Amazon S3 Batch Operations](../facts/s3.md#s3-default-encryption-change-not-retroactive).

items.front: In Amazon S3, a presigned URL is signed with role credentials that expire before the URL. When does the URL stop working?
items.extra: With temporary credentials, [the URL expires when the credential expires](../facts/s3.md#s3-presigned-url-expires-with-temporary-credentials), even when its own expiry is later.

items.front: In Amazon S3, can an event notification go directly to an SQS FIFO queue?
items.extra: To deliver S3 events to an SQS FIFO queue, [you can use Amazon EventBridge](../facts/s3.md#s3-event-notifications-no-fifo-destinations).

items.front: In S3 Intelligent-Tiering, does an object smaller than 128 KB move to a cheaper tier?
items.back: No. It stays in Frequent Access.
items.extra: An object under [128 KB](../facts/s3.md#s3-int-tiering-small-objects) is [always stored in the Frequent Access tier](../facts/s3.md#s3-int-tiering-small-objects).

items.front: In Amazon S3, which lifecycle action removes the parts of unfinished multipart uploads?
items.extra: The action [stops the multipart upload and deletes the parts](../facts/s3.md#s3-lifecycle-abort-incomplete-multipart). Complete objects stay: [no objects are deleted by this lifecycle action](../facts/s3.md#s3-lifecycle-abort-incomplete-multipart).

items.front: In Amazon S3, can you turn off Object Lock on a bucket after you turn it on?
items.extra: After you enable Object Lock, you [cannot disable S3 Object Lock or S3 Versioning](../facts/s3.md#s3-faq-object-lock-cannot-disable) for that bucket.

items.front: In Amazon S3, which tool shows storage use and activity across all accounts of an organization?
items.extra: S3 Storage Lens gives [organization-wide visibility into object storage usage](../facts/s3.md#s3-storage-lens-organization-view). S3 Inventory instead gives [a list of your objects](../facts/s3.md#s3-storage-lens-organization-view).

items.front: In Amazon S3, a single PUT can upload an object of at most {{c1::5 GB}}.
In Amazon S3, one object can be up to {{c1::50 TB}}.
items.extra: Until December 2025 the maximum was [5 TB](../facts/s3.md#s3-object-max-size). Older questions can assume that value.

items.front: In Amazon S3, Standard-IA and One Zone-IA charge a minimum storage duration of {{c1::30 days}}.
In Amazon S3, S3 Glacier Deep Archive has a minimum storage duration of {{c1::180 days}}.
In Amazon S3, Standard-IA bills each object as at least {{c1::128 KB}}.
In Amazon S3, an Expedited retrieval of a smaller object from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval typically takes {{c1::1–5 minutes}}.
In Amazon S3, a Bulk retrieval from S3 Glacier Deep Archive completes {{c1::within 48 hours}}.
In Amazon S3, a presigned URL from the AWS CLI or an SDK can be valid for up to {{c1::7 days}}.
